en.title: Minimum Index Distance Between a Person and a Cake
en.description:
In the array, 0 is an empty spot, 1 is a person, and 2 is a cake. Find the minimum absolute index difference between any person and any cake; return −1 if either kind is missing. This is not about assigning a different cake to each person.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains the array. 1≤n≤200000, and elements are only 0, 1, or 2.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 2; 2; -1. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: While scanning, keep the most recent index of a person and of a cake; whenever you meet a nonzero element, pair it with the most recent element of the other kind.
